text: Stephanie, your abstract was received last week. Two things have to be corrected before it goes out.
The first line says we analyzed the data. In this journal the methods are always written in the passive.
So it should be: the data were analyzed at three centers.
Exactly. And the second point: it is not clear when the protocol was approved.
It was approved in March, and it has been updated once since then.
Put that in one sentence and send it back today.
It will be submitted before the end of the day.
The study was conducted at three hospitals.
The protocol has been updated twice this year.
The report must be submitted by Friday.
Every chart is reviewed by a second doctor.
The patient was discharged two days after surgery.

Before we start, a short summary of the new protocol. Patients are assessed in the emergency room within ten minutes of arrival. Blood is collected immediately, and the results are sent directly to the surgical team. If surgery is needed, the family is informed before the patient goes up. After the operation, every chart is reviewed by a second doctor, not by the one who operated. That part is new, and it was added after the audit last year. The protocol was written by a group of six people, and it has been updated three times since March. The current version is on the intranet. If you are using a printed copy, throw it away.

Good afternoon. I am calling about the manuscript that was submitted to us in April. It has been reviewed by two specialists, and both reports are now with the editor. The methods section was praised, but the discussion was considered too long. The paper will not be rejected. It will be sent back to you with a request for revision, and you will be given six weeks. One practical point: the English was flagged by one of the reviewers. It is not a reason for rejection, but the text should be checked by a native speaker before it is resubmitted.
